new_kensington_city.notes: Median home construction year 1952; ~65% detached single-family. Income figure is latest ACS estimate as reported in search summary.

lower_burrell_city.notes: Income is 2024 ACS per Data USA; another source reports $86,462.

zcta_15068.notes: ACS 2024 5-year per Census Reporter (±$4,013 income, ±2.1 age). Land area ~45 sq mi. ZCTA also covers parts of Upper Burrell/Plum-adjacent areas.

economy.name: New Kensington Advanced Manufacturing Park
economy.text: Former Alcoa New Kensington Works (Alcoa began production here in 1891; plant closed 1971; later Schreiber Industrial Park). ~70 acres / ~1M sq ft spanning New Kensington and Arnold. Redevelopment Authority bought it in 2018; WCIDC–RIDC joint venture acquired it Oct. 18, 2023.

economy.name: Re:Build Manufacturing
economy.text: Anchor tenant in 175,000 sq ft at the park (expandable to 750,000). Phase 1 complete June 2024; company said it could employ 300 by 2026. Launched Re:Build Battery Solutions in New Kensington in January 2025.

economy.name: PA SITES grant – Buildings 37 & 38
economy.text: Gov. Shapiro announced a $6,984,906 PA SITES grant (May 6, 2025) to RIDC to rehab ~130,000 sq ft in Buildings 37 and 38; plus $6M Business in Our Sites funding for water, stormwater and electrical upgrades.

economy.name: Arconic Technology Center
economy.text: Arconic (spun off from Alcoa in 2016) operates its R&D Technology Center at 100 Technical Drive, New Kensington – a long-standing major employer.

economy.name: Corridor of Innovation (Fifth Avenue)
economy.text: Five-block Fifth Avenue revitalization seeded by a $150,000 Invent Penn State grant that leveraged $3M+; won PA-APA 'Great Transformation' recognition. Anchored by The Corner (701 Fifth Ave) and WCCC's center.

economy.name: Digital Foundry at New Kensington
economy.text: 15,044 sq ft advanced-manufacturing/Industry 4.0 lab on Fifth Ave, opened June 1, 2022 (funded in part by $5.5M from the Richard King Mellon Foundation). In March 2026 Penn State moved it and the New Kensington LaunchBox under the Office of the Senior VP for Research, keeping it running despite the campus closure.

economy.name: The Corner / Corner LaunchBox
economy.text: 4,725 sq ft co-working and entrepreneurial center at Fifth Ave & Seventh St, opened Dec. 6, 2017; memberships from $150/month.

economy.name: Fifth Avenue Commons
economy.text: 11,476 sq ft of office space marketed within the Corridor of Innovation.

economy.name: Olde Towne Overhaul
economy.text: Private developer (Mike Malcanas) that has bought and restored ~20 abandoned downtown buildings, operates Voodoo Brewery New Kensington and backs Fridays on Fifth.

economy.name: Penn State New Kensington campus reuse – PSU (Re)New Kensington
economy.text: Economic Growth Connection of Westmoreland, Penn State, the county and Community Foundation launched a visioning process in June 2026 (survey June 23–Aug. 14; open house Aug. 11, 2026). Property not sold; no developer chosen. Campus closes after spring 2027.

economy.name: Riverview Plaza (Tarentum Bridge Rd)
economy.text: Former Kmart site (closed 2019, demolished 2021) redeveloped with Aldi, Harbor Freight (January 2025), Starbucks (Feb. 25, 2025) and Wingstop.

economy.name: Lower Burrell business growth
economy.text: Mayor Chris Fabry said in 2026 seven businesses opened or were about to open, incl. MW Mechanical at former Hillcrest VW, Gio's Restaurant, and Tractor Supply (108 Greensburg Rd); Western PA Credit Union bought the former PNC site at Hillcrest Shopping Center.

economy.name: Hillcrest Shopping Center sale
economy.text: New York-based Nassimi Realty bought Lower Burrell's Hillcrest Shopping Center (Leechburg & Wildlife Lodge roads) at auction for over $3.78M (starting bid $1.14M) in 2024.

economy.name: Horizon Market – downtown grocery
economy.text: Small-scale grocery opened Dec. 10, 2025 at 912 Seventh St, ending downtown New Kensington's food-desert status.

economy.name: Stewart Elementary redevelopment (Lower Burrell)
economy.text: Burrell SD sold the 8.44-acre Stewart site (2800 Leechburg Rd) for $1 to developer David Ziccarelli in February 2026 for 46 duplex-style condos (min. 40 units at $275K); city donating ~1.6 more acres.

food_and_culture.name: Voodoo Brewing – New Kensington
food_and_culture.text: Brewpub in a restored downtown building run by Olde Towne Overhaul; hub for concerts, events and Fridays on Fifth; includes the Red Dragon Lounge.

food_and_culture.name: Strange Roots New Kensington
food_and_culture.text: Third location of Strange Roots Experimental Ales (wild/experimental beers), in a building owned by the Vigilante family.

food_and_culture.name: Common Oven Pizza Co.
food_and_culture.text: Wood-fired artisan pizza inside Strange Roots New Kensington; frequently named among the area's best pizza.

food_and_culture.name: botL
food_and_culture.text: Cocktail bar and restaurant ranked among the top-rated places to eat in New Kensington.

food_and_culture.name: Jillian's Restaurant
food_and_culture.text: Farm-to-table restaurant in Parnassus profiled by Pittsburgh Magazine; reservations via Resy.

food_and_culture.name: Taqueria El Pastorcito
food_and_culture.text: Popular al pastor taco food truck that opened a brick-and-mortar downtown.

food_and_culture.name: Ash Taphouse
food_and_culture.text: Wood-fired kitchen and full bar in the former Beermuda; newcomer to the 2026 Restaurant Ramble.

food_and_culture.text: Family-owned, PA Certified Organic roaster and cafe; Fair Trade/organic beans; Restaurant Ramble regular.

food_and_culture.text: Homemade pies, all-day breakfast, take-home meals; owner Jim Rennick (formerly The Fruitful Kitchen).

food_and_culture.name: Lucky Duck Candy Company

news_2025_2026.headline: Re:Build launches Re:Build Battery Solutions in New Kensington
news_2025_2026.text: The contract manufacturer anchoring the former Alcoa site launched a battery engineering/manufacturing company based at its 175,000 sq ft New Kensington plant.

news_2025_2026.headline: New Kensington-Arnold board limits possible tax increase
news_2025_2026.text: The school board voted unanimously not to exceed its state index for 2025-26; the preliminary budget proposed a 3-mill increase.

news_2025_2026.headline: Starbucks opens at Riverview Plaza
news_2025_2026.text: Drive-thru Starbucks opened Feb. 25 on Tarentum Bridge Road, following Harbor Freight's January opening at the former Kmart site; Wingstop also coming.

news_2025_2026.headline: Westmoreland Transit updates Route 14
news_2025_2026.text: Route 14 serving Lower Burrell, New Kensington, Arnold and Pittsburgh Mills got a revised schedule effective February 2025.

news_2025_2026.headline: $7M PA SITES grant for New Kensington Advanced Manufacturing Park
news_2025_2026.text: Gov. Shapiro awarded RIDC $6.98M to rehab ~130,000 sq ft in Buildings 37 and 38 of the former Alcoa works.

news_2025_2026.headline: Penn State trustees vote to close Penn State New Kensington
news_2025_2026.text: Trustees voted 25-8 on May 22 to close seven Commonwealth campuses, including New Kensington, after the spring 2027 semester.

news_2025_2026.headline: Burrell's Stewart Elementary closes; grades reconfigured
news_2025_2026.text: Starting 2025-26, Bon Air serves K-4 and Huston houses grades 5-8 after the board's 9-0 vote to close the nearly century-old Stewart Elementary.

news_2025_2026.headline: New Kensington fire companies consolidate; Parnassus station to close
news_2025_2026.text: Council recognized the merger of three volunteer companies into Citizens Volunteer Fire Company No. 1; the Parnassus station on Freeport Street is recommended for sale.

news_2025_2026.headline: Arnold and New Kensington American Legion posts merge
news_2025_2026.text: Declining membership led Arnold Post 684 and New Kensington Post 347 to form the Ar-Ken American Legion Post 347.

news_2025_2026.headline: Horizon Market ends downtown New Kensington food desert
news_2025_2026.text: A small-scale grocery opened Dec. 10 at 912 Seventh St. in the former Molnor Antiques building.

news_2025_2026.headline: Lower Burrell Tractor Supply pushed to spring
news_2025_2026.text: The store at 108 Greensburg Road, originally slated for November 2025, planned a late-March soft opening and mid-April grand opening.

news_2025_2026.headline: Lower Burrell council reorganizes for 2026
news_2025_2026.text: Council reappointed City Manager Gregory Primm for 2026-27 and renewed its Alle-Kiski Intergovernmental Council agreement.

news_2025_2026.headline: Burrell sells Stewart School site for housing
news_2025_2026.text: The board approved a $1 sale of the 8.44-acre Stewart property to developer David Ziccarelli for 46 duplex-style condos, expected to generate about a mill of taxes.

news_2025_2026.headline: Penn State realigns Digital Foundry and LaunchBox under research office
news_2025_2026.text: The New Kensington innovation spaces moved under the Office of the Senior VP for Research to secure long-term support.

news_2025_2026.headline: Arnold police get body cameras
news_2025_2026.text: Mayor Shannon Santucci secured body-worn cameras; DA Nicole Ziccarelli's office paid toward them from drug-forfeiture funds.
news_2025_2026.date_note: month inferred from article sequence – verify

news_2025_2026.headline: Fifth annual Restaurant Ramble
news_2025_2026.text: Eleven downtown eateries, including newcomers Ash Taphouse, Begonia Bistro and Lucky Duck Candy Co., took part March 28.

news_2025_2026.headline: Lower Burrell approves debt for sewer project
news_2025_2026.text: At an April 29 special meeting council approved Ordinance #2-2026 to borrow for a sewer project, 4-0.

news_2025_2026.headline: Fridays on Fifth returns with October date added
news_2025_2026.text: The downtown street festival runs the fourth Friday April-October 2026.

news_2025_2026.headline: Lower Burrell officials press for more new businesses
news_2025_2026.text: Mayor Chris Fabry cited seven new or imminent businesses including Gio's Restaurant, MW Mechanical and Tractor Supply.

news_2025_2026.headline: Community visioning launches for Penn State New Kensington site
news_2025_2026.text: The Economic Growth Connection opened a survey (June 23) and pop-up meetings at Fridays on Fifth to gather ideas for reusing the campus.

news_2025_2026.headline: Public open house on PSU New Kensington campus future
news_2025_2026.text: An Aug. 11 open house in the campus auditorium sought input; officials stress the property is not sold and no developer is chosen.

news_2025_2026.headline: PRT proposes new New Kensington–Highlands Mall bus route
news_2025_2026.text: PRT's final Bus Line Redesign proposal adds 7-day N3 service linking New Kensington, Arnold, Tarentum, Brackenridge and Natrona Heights; comments due Sept. 30.

news_2025_2026.headline: Residents raise data center concerns at New Kensington council
news_2025_2026.text: Voice of Westmoreland members asked about data center talks; Mayor Tom Guzzo said the city has none and signed no NDAs, and promised public forums if any arise.
